Sony Pictures Television self-financed S.W.A.T. Exiles, the Shemar Moore spinoff, as sole producer and distributor after CBS ended the original in May 2025, TV president Katherine Pope told TheWrap. Shopping it first would have cost the stages and the crew, so Sony greenlit 10 episodes days after the finale and sold it to Starz over a year later. Sony has renewed a second season without a Starz commitment; Starz will decide on its own season two based on new subscribers and engagement. Pope said the model only works on a show "produced at a number," not a $15 million-an-episode series.
Potential Talent Implication: When the studio fronts the money itself, a star and crew keep working instead of waiting years for a buyer, but only on a show made at a fixed number, with the platform's terms set after the risk is taken.
The Facts
  • Original: S.W.A.T. ran eight seasons on CBS, co-produced by Sony Pictures TV and CBS Studios; CBS reversed cancellations after seasons 6 and 7; the finale aired May 2025.
  • CBS passed on the spinoff because it had newer franchises in development (Pope).
  • Sony gave S.W.A.T. Exiles a 10-episode order in May 2025, days after the finale, as sole producer and distributor, keeping the Los Angeles sets and crew.
  • Showrunner: Jason Ning, under an overall deal with Sony. Executive producer Neal Moritz.
  • Distributor: Starz, landed "over a year after Sony's green light." Premieres Friday, September 25, 2026.
  • Sony renewed season two without Starz's commitment. Starz president Alison Hoffman: a season-two decision rests on the show's ability to "attract new subscribers, deepen engagement among existing viewers."
  • Pope: "The No. 1 thing about this model is it has to be able to be produced at a number... It's a big number. It's a lot of risk, but... it's not $15 million dollars an episode."
  • Pope: "TV used to be very much a deficit business and a risk-based business, and we got to... streaming deals where you didn't have to take on risk."
  • Pope said the per-season production number stayed essentially the same season after season.

  • Laika's stop-motion Wildwood (Travis Knight) releases through Fathom Entertainment on Oct. 23.
  • Black Bear's Katie Anderson: "exactly the kind of bold, ambitious event film Black Bear is passionate about bringing to audiences."

Meta's $1,299 VR Glasses Launch With 3D Versions of Disney, HBO Max and Lionsgate Films
Meta's glasses will stream 3D cuts of The Avengers and Black Panther and VR-enhanced Infinity War and A New Hope, while James Cameron's Lightstorm Vision makes new "first time in 3D" films.
Meta unveiled $1,299 VR glasses at Meta Connect on Wednesday, shipping next spring, with what it called the first IMAX-certified VR display. At launch they will stream 3D versions of Disney's The Avengers and Black Panther, VR-enhanced versions of Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope, 3D titles from the Peacock, HBO Max and Paramount+ libraries, and select Lionsgate films. James Cameron's Lightstorm Vision is developing "first time in 3D" blockbusters for next year. Meta also has immersive sports deals with the NBA, MLB and ESPN. No terms were disclosed.
Potential Talent Implication: Disney, Lionsgate and three streamers are licensing 3D and VR versions of finished films to Meta, and whether that money reaches a profit participant turns on how the original contract treats new formats and versions.
The Facts
  • Device: Meta VR glasses, $1,299; unveiled at Meta Connect (Wednesday); ships next spring. Five times lighter than Quest 3; compute and battery in a tethered puck; up to three hours of media playback.
  • Display: 5K micro-OLED; "first IMAX-certified VR device" (Meta); Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos.
  • Film content: 3D versions of Disney's The Avengers and Black Panther; VR-enhanced Avengers: Infinity War and Star Wars: A New Hope; 3D features from Peacock, HBO Max and Paramount+ libraries; select Lionsgate titles.
  • New production: James Cameron's Lightstorm Vision developing "first time in 3D" blockbusters for next year.
  • Sports: deals with NBA, MLB, ESPN and others, starting with college football.
  • Games: more than 75 at launch; Xbox Cloud Gaming support.
  • Mark Zuckerberg: "There's really nothing else like this. It is a glimpse of the future."
  • Andrew Bosworth (Meta CTO): "You get a private cinema, a game console, and a computer."
  • Terms of the content deals: not disclosed.
